== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''' was baptised at Dundonald, Ayrshire, on 12 Jun 1733. The parish register names his mother as Barbara.<ref name="FMP1" /> Because the entry records a baptism rather than a birth, his birth is placed before that date, and Dundonald is inferred from the baptism rather than independently recorded.

=== Dundonald family assessment ===

[[Stevenson-14560|Barbara Stevenson]] is the confidently identified mother of [[Glasgow-4101|William Glasgow]], assessed at 99% subjective confidence. His retained Findmypast transcript records a Dundonald baptism on 12 June 1733 and explicitly names Barbara Stevenson as mother (OPR 590/1, item 3, p.82; SCOT/OPR/BAP/3536725). FamilySearch XYZB-Z9Z concerns this same 1733 child. The two indexes represent one underlying register, not independent historical corroboration.

Select [[Glasgow-3586|William Glasgow]], the weaver at Achenyeards named as Jean’s father in the 1 October 1732 Dundonald baptism, as [[Glasgow-4101|William Glasgow]]’s possible father at 52% subjective confidence. The children share the uncommon surname and parish, their entries occur on nearby pages of the same register, and the boy’s William name agrees with the proposed father. The proposed father’s association with Barbara Stevenson is tree-derived; no inspected marriage or entry naming both parents corroborates that pairing. The whole father proposition remains an indirect household reconstruction.

The 1733 transcript has no father field or residence; absence from a transcript does not establish what the manuscript contains or prove illegitimacy. The 1732 transcript names William, weaver at Achenyeards, but no mother. Their baptisms are only 254 days apart, about eight and a half months: close spacing weakens a routine successive-infant-birth interpretation, while unknown birth dates and possible delayed baptism leave the proposed siblings compatible. Do not manufacture birth dates to resolve it. Another Glasgow father, a different Barbara Stevenson, and two separate local families remain alternatives. Barbara’s identification with her own 1733 citation is strong; the adult couple and cross-child father assignment are separate inferences. Jean’s transcript names no mother, and shared maternity of the two children remains unproved. The earlier Ayrshire William accounts [[Glasgow-1055]], [[Glasgow-3288]] and [[Glasgow-1061]] remain compatible wider comparisons; estimated ages or missing family details do not exclude them. No record links this father to any of their birth families, so no upstream father is selected. Identification of this child with later newspaper, maritime or American Williams remains unproved.  Original register images have not been inspected for this assessment.<ref>[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3536725&tab=this Findmypast retained transcript: William, 12 June 1733, Dundonald OPR590/1 item3 p.82; mother Barbara Stevenson; father field absent]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZB-Z9Z FamilySearch XYZB-Z9Z: the same 1733 baptism cited by Barbara’s existing profile; citation reused, record page not newly inspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3536699&tab=this Findmypast retained transcript: Jean, 1 October 1732, Dundonald OPR590/1 item3 p.80; father William, weaver, Achenyeards; mother absent]. Maintained transcripts and citation, not newly inspected original pages.</ref>

The baptism is the only record found for William Glasgow. A search of live WikiTree profiles found no compatible match; [[Glasgow-2426|William]] belongs to a different family and is not this person.

=== Possible William Glascoe / Glascow, 1760 defendant ===
William Glascoe is among prisoners reported sentenced to transportation after Old Bailey trials, for stealing a sack of malt from a warehouse, valued in the newspaper at £4 10s.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/35690357/ Public Ledger or Daily Register of Commerce and Intelligence, 1760-04-18, p.2].</ref>

The newspaper uses Glascoe; the associated Old Bailey case uses Glascow. The case association does not establish the defendant’s origin, family or identity with the later Maryland man.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4101]]. The recorded before 1733-06-12 birth at Dundonald, Ayrshire, Scotland is chronologically compatible. The newspaper gives no family or individual identifier connecting this occurrence to Glasgow-4101.

=== Possible William Glasgow, master of the Lady Forbes ===
William Glasgow is named as master of the Lady Forbes in the Sutton shipping casualty report.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050136699/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1768-01-23, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395700744/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1768-02-06, p.2].</ref>

The January 1768 report says the rum-carrying Lady Forbes, bound for Waterford, was driven ashore near Sutton and the crew were saved. The ship’s Glasgow home port does not give William’s birthplace. No identity with the later brig William or Falmouth master follows.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4101]]. Birth before 12 June 1733; Dundonald baptism. Chronologically compatible, but no master, vessel or maritime identification.

=== Possible William Glasgow, Philadelphia and Charles-Town postal lists, 1759–1771 ===
William Glasgow, Cecil County, is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39399295/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1759-08-09, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in February 1763.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39390517/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1763-02-24, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in October 1765.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39405824/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1765-10-10, p.4].</ref>

William Glasgow is separately listed in the Charles-Town, Maryland, post-office letters notice headed 1 October 1771, beside an entry for John Glasgow of West Nottingham.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41041559/ Maryland Gazette, 1771-10-24, p.3].</ref>

Cecil County explicitly qualifies the 1759 entry only. In 1763 "Pennsylvania" follows James Gillispie; in 1765 "Forks of Delaware" qualifies William Greenlee, not William Glasgow. The entries may concern different men, and co-listing with John in 1771 does not prove a family relationship.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4101]]. Birth before 12 June 1733, Dundonald, permits these dates; no Cecil County or postal identification.
